The Induced Smoothed Lasso

Source: R/islasso.R
islasso.Rd

Fits regression models with a smoothed lasso (or elastic-net) penalty under the induced smoothing paradigm, which yields point estimates, standard errors and Wald tests for all the coefficients.

Usage

islasso(
  formula,
  family = gaussian,
  lambda,
  alpha = 1,
  data,
  weights,
  subset,
  offset,
  unpenalized,
  contrasts = NULL,
  control = is.control()
)

islasso.fit(
  X,
  y,
  family = gaussian,
  lambda,
  alpha = 1,
  intercept = FALSE,
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  unpenalized = NULL,
  control = is.control()
)

Arguments

formula

a symbolic description of the model (see stats::formula()).

family

the error distribution and link function: a family object, a family function or its name. Any family accepted by stats::glm() can be used, for instance gaussian(), binomial() (links logit, probit, cauchit, log, cloglog), poisson(), Gamma(), inverse.gaussian(), the quasi* families and MASS::negative.binomial() with known theta.

lambda

the tuning parameter (a non-negative number). If missing, it is chosen by cross-validation with glmnet::cv.glmnet() (see nfolds and seed in is.control()). With lambda = 0 the model is not penalized (same estimates as glm()) and the model matrix must have full column rank: aliased terms (NA coefficients in glm()) give an error.

alpha

the elastic-net mixing parameter, \(0 \le \alpha \le 1\): alpha = 1 is the lasso, alpha = 0 the ridge penalty.

data

an optional data frame containing the variables in the model.

weights

optional vector of prior weights.

subset

an optional vector specifying a subset of observations.

offset

an optional offset in the linear predictor.

unpenalized

names or indices (with respect to the columns of the model matrix without intercept) of the coefficients left unpenalized. The intercept is never penalized.

contrasts

an optional list of contrasts for the factors (see stats::model.matrix()).

control

a list of control parameters, see is.control().

X, y

for islasso.fit(): the model matrix (without the column of ones) and the response.

intercept

for islasso.fit(): logical, should an (unpenalized) intercept be included?

Value

An object of class "islasso", a list with components including

coefficients, se

estimates and standard errors on the original scale;

dispersion

the dispersion parameter;

fitted.values, linear.predictors, residuals, weights, prior.weights

as in stats::glm() (residuals are the working residuals and weights the working weights);

deviance, null.deviance, aic, rank, df.residual, df.null

deviance-based summaries; rank is the effective number of parameters, the sum of the pseudo hat values;

converged, iter

convergence flag and number of iterations;

lambda, alpha, family, control, call, formula, terms, model, data, xlevels, contrasts, offset, y

the inputs;

internal

other internal quantities (full covariance matrix, pseudo hat values hi, gradient, mixture weights, standardisation constants, ...).

Details

For a fixed \(\lambda\) the lasso estimating equation \(-X^\top W (z - X\beta) + \lambda\,\mathrm{sign}(\beta) = 0\) is not smooth. The induced smoothing (IS) approach (Brown and Wang, 2005) replaces \(\mathrm{sign}(\beta_j)\) by its expectation under the approximate sampling distribution of the estimator, modelled as the mixture \(c\,N(0,1) + (1-c)\,N(0,10^{-10})\) of a continuous component and a component concentrated at zero: $$P_j = c\,\{2\Phi(\beta_j/s_j) - 1\} + (1-c)\,\{2\Phi(10^5 \beta_j/s_j) - 1\},$$ where \(s_j\) is the standard error of \(\hat\beta_j\). The smoothed equation \(\tilde U(\beta) = -X^\top W(z - X\beta) + \lambda\{\alpha P + (1-\alpha)\beta\} = 0\) admits the derivative \(\tilde U'(\beta) = X^\top W X + \lambda\,\mathrm{diag}\{\alpha P' + 1 - \alpha\}\), and the covariance matrix is obtained by the sandwich formula \(V = \phi\,\tilde U'^{-1} X^\top W X\, \tilde U'^{-1}\). Point estimates and standard errors are computed alternately until the standard errors stabilise.

At fixed standard errors, \(\tilde U\) is the gradient of a smooth convex function, which is minimised by a monotone majorise-minimise algorithm (default) or by Newton's method with line search (inner = "newton" in is.control()). When the number of columns exceeds twice the number of observations, the linear algebra uses the Woodbury identity, with cost \(O(n^2 p)\) instead of \(O(p^3)\). Generalised linear models are fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares, so any family with the usual components (linkinv, mu.eta, variance, dev.resids) is supported.

With stand = TRUE (default in is.control()) the covariates are standardised (weighted mean and standard deviation with divisor \(\sum w\), as in glmnet) and the penalty acts on the standardised coefficients; the results are reported on the original scale. The scale of lambda is that of the deviance: \(\lambda = \sum_i w_i\,\lambda_{glmnet}\).

Since the smoothed penalty is never exactly flat, no estimate is exactly zero: the Wald statistics, rather than the point estimates, are used to judge which covariates matter. For coefficients whose estimate is shrunk to (practically) zero the induced-smoothing fixed point drives the standard error towards zero as well, while the Wald ratio stays stable: their standard errors depend on the convergence tolerance and should not be used to build confidence intervals. See vignette("islasso-methodology", package = "islasso").

References

Cilluffo G., Sottile G., La Grutta S., Muggeo V.M.R. (2020). The induced smoothed lasso: a practical framework for hypothesis testing in high dimensional regression. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 29(3), 765–777. doi:10.1177/0962280219842890

Sottile G., Cilluffo G., Muggeo V.M.R. (2019). The R package islasso: estimation and hypothesis testing in lasso regression. Technical report. doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.16360.11521

Brown B.M., Wang Y.G. (2005). Standard errors and covariance matrices for smoothed rank estimators. Biometrika, 92(1), 149–158. doi:10.1093/biomet/92.1.149

Examples

n <- 100; p <- 50
beta <- c(rep(1, 5), rep(0, p - 5))
sim1 <- simulXy(n = n, p = p, beta = beta, seed = 1, family = gaussian())
o <- islasso(y ~ ., data = sim1$data, family = gaussian(), lambda = 10)
summary(o, pval = 0.05)
#> 
#> Call:
#> islasso(formula = y ~ ., family = gaussian(), lambda = 10, data = sim1$data)
#> 
#> Residuals:
#>      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
#> -1.62155 -0.60848 -0.04476  0.51511  1.79945 
#> 
#>             Estimate Std. Error     Df z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept) -0.11060    0.09886  1.000  -1.119    0.263    
#> X1           0.82242    0.10738  1.000   7.659 1.87e-14 ***
#> X2           0.95762    0.10829  1.000   8.843  < 2e-16 ***
#> X3           0.81484    0.10836  1.000   7.520 5.50e-14 ***
#> X4           0.99564    0.11054  1.000   9.007  < 2e-16 ***
#> X5           0.91294    0.10743  1.000   8.498  < 2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 0.9772461)
#> 
#>     Null deviance: 657.721  on 99.00  degrees of freedom
#> Residual deviance:  70.928  on 72.58  degrees of freedom
#> AIC: 306.28
#> Lambda: 10
#> 
#> Number of IS iterations: 238
#> 
head(coef(o))
#> (Intercept)          X1          X2          X3          X4          X5 
#>  -0.1106006   0.8224221   0.9576181   0.8148399   0.9956382   0.9129428 
logLik(o)
#> 'log Lik.' -124.7188 (df=28.4205)

# \donttest{
# lambda chosen by 5-fold cross-validation (reproducible through 'seed')
o <- islasso(y ~ ., data = sim1$data, control = is.control(seed = 1))
summary(relax.islasso(o), pval = 0.05)

# binomial
beta <- c(1, 1, 1, rep(0, p - 3))
sim2 <- simulXy(n = n, p = p, beta = beta, interc = 1, seed = 1, size = 100,
                family = binomial())
o2 <- islasso(cbind(y.success, y.failure) ~ ., data = sim2$data, family = binomial(),
              lambda = 5)
summary(o2, pval = 0.05)

#> islasso(formula = cbind(y.success, y.failure) ~ ., family = binomial(),

summary(o3, pval = 0.05)

# Gamma with log link
sim4 <- simulXy(n = n, p = p, beta = beta, interc = -1, seed = 1, dispersion = 0.1,
                family = Gamma(link = "log"))
o4 <- islasso(y ~ ., data = sim4$data, family = Gamma(link = "log"), lambda = 5)
summary(o4, pval = 0.05)
